case_32.kernel_family: stable bitonic argsort for small rows
case_32.reason: The tie-break is inverted: my_is_smaller uses `(keys == p_key) & (perm > p_perm)`, so among equal keys the entry with the LARGER original index is treated as smaller and placed first, yielding an anti-stable (index-descending) tie order. Additionally, for non-power-of-two W the padding lanes are excluded from exchanges via `(partner < W)` masking, so descending bitonic sub-stages can't move real elements into padded slots and the sort is simply wrong (e.g. row [3,1,2] yields [1,3,2]).
